attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his essay, said in his own voice.

semantics.note: Keeps 'forte', 'always will be', and the 'on their own' scope. It bundles a statement about the past with a perpetual forecast, but the firm 'always will be' makes it a scorable forecast.

contract.note: Reading 'cannot check facts' as no dependable fact-checking ability, and excluding tools, is ordinary and fair. It can only be falsified by a replicated, broad demonstration, which matches a universal claim with no deadline.

evidence.note: A tool-free factual-recall benchmark that includes GPT models. It measures parametric recall, not fact verification, so it does not meet the contradiction condition.
SelfCheckGPT (2023) detects some hallucinations through repeated sampling on WikiBio. The evaluation is narrow and the method is a procedure, not dependable standalone fact-checking.

reviews.rationale: This is an open-ended forecast with no deadline. Neither item shows replicated, broadly dependable fact-checking by a standalone GPT, so the early-resolution rule is not met. Continued failures cannot confirm a claim about all future models, so it stays unresolved.

attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence in his essay.

semantics.note: 'Advanced cognitive abilities attributed to' is a fair paraphrase of 'fancy cognitive things... rumored to do'. The 'essentially none' quantifier is kept.

contract.note: Counting cognitive-reflection and conjunction-fallacy reasoning as covered abilities is the evaluator's choice. Still, reasoning was widely claimed for GPT-4 in March 2023, so this is an ordinary reading of the broad wording. The result turns on that choice.

evidence.note: Peer-reviewed study with GPT-4 runs dated March 2023. On new items over many trials, GPT-4 was near-perfect on cognitive-reflection and Linda/Bill problems, so controlled competence held up on several reasoning tasks.
Documents arithmetic and planning failures in an early pre-release GPT-4. Consistent with some abilities failing, but it is not the released model.

reviews.rationale: The claim is a near-total dismissal. Controlled March 2023 experiments (e3) show robust GPT-4 competence on several cognitive reasoning tasks beyond isolated demonstrations, which meets the contradiction condition. Failures elsewhere (e4) do not save 'essentially none'. The verdict depends on counting these reasoning tests among the rumored abilities.

attribution.note: Marcus cites Sap's work but asserts the conclusion himself ('confirmed what we suspected'), so it is his endorsed claim.

semantics.note: The proposition drops the attribution to Sap's findings, but the contract adds it back. The core claim, that mastery is a myth, is kept.

contract.note: Reading 'mastered' as robust competence across controlled mental-state tasks, for models of the time, is ordinary and fair.

evidence.note: Sap et al. extension, posted April 3, 2023. gpt-4-0314 scores about 59% on ToMi mental-state questions, far below mastery, which matches the attributed finding.
Kosinski reports 95% for GPT-4 on 40 classic false-belief tasks. This is genuine positive evidence, but the task set is narrow and does not show robust mastery.

reviews.rationale: Sap's investigation from the period found GPT-4 near chance on ToMi mental-state questions, which is incompatible with robust mastery and matches what Marcus attributed to it. Kosinski's narrower positive results do not establish robust generalization.

attribution.note: Marcus's own forecast in his essay.

semantics.note: 'A safe bet' plus an unqualified 'will' is high confidence, so this is a scorable forecast. No deadline was given.

contract.note: Requiring matched, blinded comparisons against the original GPT-4 is fair. Reading 'convincing sounding prose' as fluent, plausible prose is ordinary.

evidence.note: OpenAI's own disclosure. It compares against GPT-4o, not original GPT-4, using selected examples.
One unblinded reviewer prompt, with an unspecified GPT-4 configuration. Suggestive only.
Blinded human ratings favour GPT-5's academic writing, but the baseline is inconsistently named GPT-4 or GPT-4o.

reviews.rationale: GPT-5 has been released, but no item is a reliable, version-identified comparison with original GPT-4 on convincing prose. The evidence leans in favour without meeting the contract's requirements, so the early-resolution rule is not satisfied.
